name: Tile-Aligned Five-Encoder Gated-Attention MIL
summary: Each patient's slides form a spatially aligned tile bag across all five frozen H&E encoders, excluding all clinical and receptor variables. Within nested training folds, per-encoder tile features are standardized and PCA-compressed before a neural network performs per-tile encoder fusion and gated-attention pooling to predict class-weighted PAM50 subtypes. Evaluation uses repeated nested patient-level and site-held-out cross-validation against null baselines and the patient-mean logistic reference. Patient-level, per-class, and site-held-out bootstrap confidence intervals determine whether H&E morphology yields broad, partial, site-confounded, or insufficient PAM50 predictability.
preprocessing: Assert zero clinical, immunohistochemistry receptor (er, pr, her2), histological_type, age, stage, RNA-derived, or site variables enter any feature tensor; exclude the 259 unlabelled patients from supervised fitting and all scoring.

Aggregate all slides per labelled patient (802 patients, 1132 slides) into a single patient-level tile bag while preserving exact spatial tile-index alignment across UNI2-h, CONCH-Z, Virchow2, MUSK, and H-Optimus-1.

Strictly inside each training fold, apply L2 normalization and z-score standardization per encoder, then fit a 128-component randomized PCA per encoder on training-fold tiles only to equalize native dimensions (768 to 2560) before projecting validation/test tiles.
Compute inverse-prevalence class weights for LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 strictly from each training fold's labelled patient counts.

training.convergence_check: Log epoch training loss and inner-validation macro-F1/loss curves; require early-stopping trigger or non-improving trailing-5-epoch loss slope before outer-fold scoring.

required_comparators: Majority-class null classifier fit on identical outer training folds
Stratified class-prior null classifier fit on identical outer training folds
Inner-tuned class-weighted patient_mean_logreg single-encoder H&E reference evaluated on identical 802 labelled patients and outer fold assignments

metrics: Out-of-fold four-class macro-F1 and paired macro-F1 gain over majority-class and stratified class-prior chance baselines with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs
Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference versus inner-tuned single-encoder patient_mean_logreg reference with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Proportion of class-prior multi-class log-loss (Shannon entropy) explained out-of-fold with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Macro and per-class one-vs-rest AUROC plus per-class precision, recall, and F1 across LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs
Site-held-out grouped CV macro-F1 and paired macro-F1 gain over chance across the 19 collection sites with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Fold-wise training convergence verification rate and trailing-epoch loss slope summary
allowed_conclusions: Select exactly one of the four objective conclusions—Broad predictability (95% CIs above chance in both patient and site-held-out CV and for all four classes), Partial predictability (overall 95% CIs above chance in both CVs but at least one class fails), Site-confounded predictability (beats chance in patient CV but site-held-out paired 95% CI includes or falls below zero), or Insufficient evidence (patient-level paired 95% CI over chance includes or falls below zero)—and additionally state whether tile-aligned multi-encoder MIL outperforms the patient-mean logistic reference; scoped strictly to standalone frozen-encoder H&E prediction in TCGA-BRCA without claiming clinical incremental value or biological mechanism.
rationale: Mean pooling dilutes focal tumour cues with stroma, while single encoders capture incomplete morphology. Tile-aligned gating across five encoders with attention MIL isolates diagnostic regions. Fold-internal PCA, balanced class weighting, tile dropout, and seed ensembling counteract high dimensionality, minority Her2 imbalance, and technical site confounding.
